title: A Computational Workflow for Cost-Effective Synthesis of Inorganic Materials: Integrating Thermodynamics, Cellular Automata, Machine Learning, and Commercial Databases
experiments_summary: A synthesis recipe recommendation experiment was conducted for Ca2SiO4, targeting its use as a naval coating material. The chemical search space was restricted to elements Ca, Si, O, C, N, H, Al, and B, with a synthesis temperature range of 800–1600°C. The workflow was executed in three modular stages: (1) a design module that constructed a chemical space using the Materials Project and JANAF databases, applied the SISSO-learned descriptor to estimate temperature-dependent energetic properties, used the reaction-network library to select thermodynamically favorable recipes, and cross-checked reactant commercial availability via PubChem; (2) a simulation module based on the React-CA cellular automaton framework, which identified and scored all possible reactions within each recipe's chemical system, then simulated each recipe through thermodynamic stages across multiple generations to estimate product yields; and (3) an analysis module that integrated thermodynamic simulation outputs with commercial supplier data from ChemSpace and applied the CrabNet AI model to estimate physicochemical descriptors such as solubility and volatility. Economic efficiency metrics were computed by jointly considering thermodynamic performance and average market prices of reactants at minimum 95% purity. A total of 261 synthesis recipes involving 36 commercially accessible reactants were evaluated, and the three best-performing recipes based on economic efficiency were selected and compared across multiple evaluation metrics.
